items.title: Stacks are LIFO; queues are FIFO
items.claim: A web browser's 'back' button uses which data structure?

options.text: Stack (LIFO) — the most recent page is the first one you return to

items.reveal:
Other stack uses: function call stack (each function pushes a frame, returns pop them), expression evaluation, depth-first search, undo functionality.

Queue uses: print spoolers, BFS, message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ), CPU scheduling (round-robin), buffering in pipelines. Priority queue extends with ordering — used in Dijkstra's shortest path, OS scheduling.

The stack-based call convention is so foundational that 'stack overflow' (from recursion too deep) gave the popular Q&A site its name.
items.why: Choosing the right abstract data type clarifies the algorithm. Stack vs queue vs priority queue picks a temporal access pattern.

items.title: Latency differences
items.claim: L1 cache access takes about 1 ns. Roughly how long does a fetch from main memory take by comparison?
items.reveal:
Approximate figures (Jeff Dean's 'numbers everyone should know'): L1 cache 1 ns, main memory 100 ns, SSD 100 microseconds, disk seek 10 ms.

The ratios drive cache-friendly algorithm design.
items.why: Algorithm choice often matters less than memory layout once data exceeds cache size.

items.title: RAM is volatile; storage persists
items.claim: A computer is suddenly unplugged mid-operation. What happens to data?

options.text: Data in RAM is lost (DRAM needs refresh to retain charge); data in SSD/HDD persists. This is why crash safety requires explicit flushing (fsync) to storage

items.reveal:
DRAM cells lose charge in milliseconds without refresh. SRAM (cache) holds state while powered but is volatile. SSDs (NAND flash) and HDDs are non-volatile.

Databases use write-ahead logging (WAL): changes go to log on disk before being applied to main data structures, so a crash mid-transaction can be replayed or rolled back. Filesystems (ext4, NTFS, APFS) use journaling for similar reasons. NVRAM and persistent memory (Intel Optane, discontinued 2022) blurred the boundary briefly.
items.why: The volatile/persistent distinction shapes everything from OS design to database recovery to backup strategy.
